title: Dunn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC held the complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1 because the original complaint was transmitted to the Faith Church Commission by the Stated Clerk, not committed by Presbytery motion as BCO 15-3 requires, and because the Commission did not seek Presbytery approval of its judgment. The SJC directed Presbytery to remedy these deficiencies no later than its next Stated Meeting before further action.
first_summary: The SJC held TE Dwight Dunn's complaint against Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery administratively out of order. The original complaint had been sent to the Faith Church Commission by the Stated Clerk rather than committed by Presbytery, and the Commission denied it without obtaining Presbytery approval. The SJC directed Presbytery to remedy the deficiencies by its next Stated Meeting.
summary: The SJC held TE Dwight Dunn's complaint administratively out of order under OMSJC 9.1 and directed Presbytery to remedy the deficiencies by its next Stated Meeting before further action under OMSJC 9.2. The original complaint had been transmitted to the Faith Church Commission by the Stated Clerk, not committed by Presbytery motion as BCO 15-3 requires, and after the Commission denied it, the Commission did not seek Presbytery approval of its judgment. Because Presbytery had not acted, the SJC complaint was premature; no merits were reached.
